div.head: Rect 21.5
div.ab: [21.5] Ðis is ðeah myngung manna biwiste ⁊ eal þæt ic ær beforan ymberehte.
[21.5] quorum hoc uiaticum sit et quod supra diximus.

On sumre ðeode gebyreð winterfeorm . easter|feorm . bendform for ripe . gytfeorm for yrðe . mæðmed hreacmete . æt wudulade wæntreow . æt cornlade hreaccopp . 7 fela ðinga ðe ic getellan ne mæig . ðis is ðeah myn|gung manna bi wiste . 7 eal þæt ic ær beforan ymbe rehte
Ðis is ðeah myngung manna biwiste and eal þæt ic ær beforan ymberehte.
Dies [letzte] ist jedoch ein Memorandum der Leute-Verköstigung, sowie all was ich eben zuvor erklärt habe.
This [last] is however a memorandum of the people's food-provision, as is all that I have just explained above.

On some lands winter provisions are due, Easter provisions, a boon-meal for reaping, a ploughing-feast for ploughing, hayrick-meal [as] reward [for] cutting grass, for a load of wood one tree, for a load of corn the top of the hayrick, and many things which I may not tell, this [last] is nevertheless an admonition about watching over men, and all that I explained about before.
Yet this is an admonition concerning the provisioning of the people, and all that I have previously described.

maniyra manna biwist ‘vieler Männer Weistum’ empfiehlt Leo unrichtig, danach zweifelnd Schmid, der sonst nur ‘Ermunterung der Gutsleute zur Nahrung’ herauslesen kann. Aber mynegung kann ‘Mahnung, Erinnerung’, biwist ‘Nahrungs(Unterhalts)mittel’ bedeuten

Leo wrongly recommends maniyra manna biwist ‘record of custom of many men’, and after him, doubtfully, Schmid, who otherwise can only read out of it ‘encouragement of the estate people to nourishment’. But mynegung can mean ‘admonition, reminder’, biwist ‘means of nourishment (subsistence)’
